name: CHAOS-3851 explicit queue selection
$limitation: The plan proves required and exact queue concurrency input, propagation into the constructed startup budget, one process-level River client, independent groups with identical queue sets, worker-group label neutrality, visibility of live custom groups, and renderer emission of queue concurrency. It does not prove live multi-process claim distribution or autoscaler behavior; those require the integration and deployment environments.

mutations.rationale: A River worker must fail closed when deployment does not provide per-queue concurrency; accepting an empty budget would create a queue-selected process with no reviewed capacity.
The deployment map must contain exactly one capacity for every selected queue; both a missing queue and an extra queue must be rejected rather than silently changing the worker topology.

The runtime startup contract must carry the deployment's per-queue worker limit into the constructed budget; replacing it with an application default would make deployment scaling opaque and incorrect.

mutations.find: return riverWorkerProcess{client: client, family: family}, nil
mutations.replace:
_, _ = river.NewClient(
		riverpgxv5.New(postgresDatabase.pools.QueueControl),
		&river.Config{ID: cfg.WorkerInstanceID + "-duplicate", Logger: logger, Queues: queues, Schema: cfg.RiverDatabaseSchema, Workers: workers},
	)
	return riverWorkerProcess{client: client, family: family}, nil
mutations.rationale: All selected queue families must share one River client and one worker registry; a second process client would create duplicate maintenance and leadership identities inside one worker process.
Two independently scaled River groups may intentionally consume the same queue set; a queue-set uniqueness rejection would prevent valid deployment grouping even though process names remain distinct.
Worker group is an operator label, not a queue selector; changing the deployment label must preserve the selected queues and their budgets while changing only reported identity.
Operator status must include a live worker group that is absent from the checked-in manifest, so ad hoc deployment groups remain observable during rollout and autoscaling.
The Compose renderer must pass the deployment's queue concurrency to every Go worker; omitting it causes the process to fail closed or lose the reviewed capacity contract.
